findings.title: Clauses 3 and 4 silently create an exception to D-056 Eligibility gates 2 and 3 while disclaiming any D-056 amendment.
subjectClaims: D-364 accepts that D-294 trigger (b) fired and that preview-product-boundary-successor.v10 owes a successor, then says the obligation conditions no D-056 Eligibility gate.

Clause 4 says a SATISFIED re-record may proceed while that successor remains outstanding if the re-record names the successor, ground, and owner; the clause expressly admits that naming is not discharging.
The rejected alternative says no adopted text makes gates 4 and 5 wait, because the obligation arose after the D-316 gate-1 acceptance.
governingBytes: D-056's pinned turn-2 subject says all five gates must be true at the moment of the later SATISFIED cycle. Gate 2 permits only harness execution, fixture execution, or qualification measurement, and expressly says authoring of fixtures, schemas, successors, actor-joins, missing design, or still-UNDECIDED numbers is not a remainder the amendment may split.

D-056 gate 3 additionally requires each allowed remainder already to be named as a condition-4 / DR-G* obligation with an owner. Merely naming an outstanding successor inside the future SATISFIED entry does not make successor authoring an allowed gate-2 remainder and does not satisfy the already-named DR-G* condition.

D-133 preserves that exact rule: all five gates are measured for the row at the moment of the later cycle. The 2026-08-29 T2-02 acceptance establishes gate 1; it does not grandfather gates 2 and 3 against obligations that exist at the later cycle.

D-294 trigger (b) applies when a sibling changes a value the citing artifact relies on. Once D-364 holds that this test reaches v10 and that a successor is required, the owed successor is not made external to acceptance evidence merely by calling the obligations independent.

The D-294 status-token sentence cited at D-364 lines 101-102 is expressly scoped in D-294 to triggers (a) and (c), and describes a join on an already-SATISFIED row. It proves that a later obligation can coexist with an existing token; it does not authorize a row that is still OPEN to cross into SATISFIED while known successor authoring remains.

D-293 Decision 5 and D-314 item 1 omit a post-authoring successor step, but omission from that programme does not supersede D-056's gate-2 successor exclusion. D-364 itself declines to read D-314 as eliminating the later D-294 obligation, because it repeatedly says the successor remains owed.

chronologyAudit.reason: The ordering shows the trigger arose after gate 1 opened. D-056 and D-133 make gates 2 and 3 current-cycle properties, so the ordering does not establish that the later obligation is irrelevant to them.

findings.whyMustFix: Clause 3 is load-bearing for the planned D-363 SATISFIED re-record. On the draft's own broad D-294 reading, successor authoring is presently owed; D-056 expressly excludes outstanding successor authoring from the remainder a SATISFIED cycle may split. Adopting clauses 3 and 4 would therefore alter the D-056 eligibility rule while the front matter and clause 6 say D-056 is not amended. A dependent D-363 could proceed on an eligibility basis the adopted five-gate text does not permit.
requiredCorrection: Reconcile the fired D-294 successor obligation with the exact D-056 gate-2 successor exclusion and D-133's later-cycle timing rule; chronology of gate 1 is not that reconciliation.

Either discharge the successor obligation before gates 4 and 5, or expressly adopt and review a scoped successor amendment to D-056 that makes this class of D-294 maintenance successor non-blocking. Do not present the latter as a reading that leaves D-056 unamended.

If the intended theory is that this owed successor is not a remaining acceptance-evidence member, state the adopted textual basis for that classification and explain how it coexists with D-294's holding that the citing artifact relied on the changed projected values and requires a successor.

summary: OBJECT with one MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX. The functional D-294 predicate reading is applied consistently to Decisions 1 and 2; those decisions are independent; the D-363 shared-finding account is accurate; all eight v11-v14 Stage A verdicts are REJECT; the g29 and g30 trigger-(b) rulings fire while g21 and distribution-core do not; all twelve file-backed digests, nine commit ids, chronology, heading-numbering precedent, immediate readiness effect, and protected boundaries reproduce. The load-bearing gating conclusion does not: D-056 gate 2 expressly excludes successor authoring from the remainder a SATISFIED cycle may split, gate 3 requires allowed remainder already named at a DR-G* obligation, and D-133 makes those gates properties at the later cycle. D-316's earlier T2-02 acceptance fixes gate 1 but does not grandfather gates 2 and 3. Clause 4's promise to name an admittedly undischarged successor therefore cannot let D-363 proceed without either discharging it or expressly amending D-056. Separately, the stability clause says six leftover-join inputs while the table pins eight.
